root_cause.mechanism: mla_decode_fwd allocates valid_split_count with torch.empty; the gfx950 stage1 asm never writes it; Triton stage2 merges min(splits, leftover) splits -> leftover<=0 gives 0 splits, acc/e_sum = 0/0 = NaN (1..splits-1: silently wrong)
root_cause.defence: the read is gated only on num_kv_splits > 1 (no arch check) and relies on the asm writeback, which exists only in the gfx1250 packed MLA kernels; the zero-fill was dropped as dead work
conditions: non-gfx1250 GPU (gfx950): no writer of valid_split_count
leftover allocator int32 <= 0 (NaN) or < num_kv_splits (wrong values)

alternatives: gate use_valid_split_count_reduce to kernels that write valid_split_count (gfx1250) -- blind run 5 shipped this with torch.full
num_kv_splits=1 (a workaround: the reduce does not read the buffer)

validated.reproducer: stock 349/800 -> fixed 0/800 (fix_check, poisoned allocator); capsule operand recorded 8192/8192 NaN -> num_kv_splits 0/8192

notes: The NaN is deterministic for a given allocator history: the leftover int32 under valid_split_count decides (<= 0: 0/0 NaN; 1..15: wrong finite values; >= 16: correct). The capture keeps that operand's bytes, so the op capsule replays at concurrency 1. A Triton kernel has no fp64 reference: KERNEL_BUG_UNVERIFIED is the expected verdict. Upstream fix: aiter #4186 (torch.full), which reverted #4129; the e_sum > 0 guard of #6394 turns the NaN into zeros.
